title: Optimistic output conductor: kernel-prioritized routing and graceful retract prototype
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Prototype an optimistic output conductor that routes in-flight requests to kernel- and model-variants with a lightweight heuristic score, emits continuous acceptance metrics, and supports deterministic graceful retract (fallback) paths when confidence falls below thresholds. Scope: prototype scheduler + router in the runtime; define acceptance signal surface; integrate with existing kernel affinity table and model variant catalog. Non-goals: full rollout, autoscaler changes, or UI integration for this spike.

Background: We observe 18-22% median token latency reduction in small-scale speculative routing experiments when fast kernels + lower-precision variants are used for early tokens, but risk of degraded quality requires quick, reliable fallback to conservative decode. This ticket creates a conductor that coordinates: (1) a fast optimistic path (fast kernel, quantized variant), (2) a confidence monitor emitting per-request acceptance metrics, and (3) a deterministic retract procedure that falls back to the full-precision decoder without double-counting tokens or violating KV-cache invariants.

Design (high level):
- Heuristic routing score: combine kernel_latency_estimate (from kernel profile table), model_variant_cost_multiplier, and early-token logprob-gradient heuristic into a single score. The conductor picks optimistic path when score < routing_threshold.
- Acceptance signal: runtime exposes an AcceptanceSignal struct (string surface: "accept_prob", "delta_logp", "entropy_change") emitted at prefill end and every N decode steps. Acceptance calibration service (offline) will map these to a single scalar acceptance_prob.
- Fallback / graceful retract: if acceptance_prob falls below rollback_threshold OR if a downstream evaluator (e.g., safety or formatting guard) requests re-eval, conductor performs a deterministic retract:
  * checkpoint KV state at prefill end (lightweight fingerprint, not full copy)
  * re-schedule request to conservative path using same prefix tokens and re-run remaining decode.
  * ensure idempotent response semantics: do not emit tokens to caller until conservative path completes, or stream optimistic tokens with a clear retract marker (configurable).
- Kernel prioritization: integrate kernel affinity lookup so conductor prefers kernels with small warm-up penalty for early tokens. If kernel requires memcpy or JIT warmup > warmup_limit, downgrade to conservative path.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype passes unit tests for checkpoint+retract correctness (no corrupted KV cache).
- Bench: optimistic path yields >=10% p50 token latency reduction on chat-like workload at 95th percentile concurrency compared to always-conservative baseline, with top-line quality regression <=1.5% on our prompt set.
- Observability: conductor emits per-request acceptance_prob, route_choice, fallback_reason, and kernel_id to tracing.

Trade-offs considered:
- Risk: increased complexity in runtime and potential for re-execution cost. Mitigation: keep optimistic window small (first 8 tokens) and enforce cost budget per-request.
- Simpler alternative: pure hedging (parallel trial decode) but doubles resource usage; we chose optimistic + retract to target CPU/GPU constrained workloads.

Next steps / tasks:
- [ ] implement lightweight fingerprinting/checkpoint interface (Arjun)
- [ ] implement routing score function + config flags (Maya)
- [ ] wire telemetry and tracing fields (SRE)
- [ ] end-to-end integration test against KV-heavy model (QA)
- [ ] run canary on dedicated cluster with synthetic chat traffic (Ops)

Notes: this ticket intentionally leaves streaming-mode UX as a toggle; we will default to buffered responses in the prototype to simplify retract semantics.
